analysis_kind: Read-only post-study classification of frozen primary private outcomes

provenance.json_value_hash_definition: SHA256 of UTF-8 json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False, separators=(',', ':'))
provenance.source_note: Candidate source was read as JSON string data from each final trajectory, never imported or executed. Final file hashes and trajectory byte hashes were checked against frozen results.

key_findings: Five completed runs fail two scenarios solely because commit audit IDs are unsorted; their plans, built sequences, digests and other recorded outputs match.

Completed runs additionally show malformed-type errors, valid import identifier rejection, or import precedence deviations. These contradict explicit frozen contracts; error receipts contain no exception trace.

The portfolio run completing two milestones has an attempted third-milestone defect: correct digests but empty built receipts/audit IDs. One fourth-milestone case exposes this earlier defect before unsupported import.

Two early-stop sources contribute 44 future-stage failure occurrences, including one mixed earlier-defect case. These are unmet final requirements, not 44 demonstrated defects in implemented future features.

The stage 0-only portfolio source passes all 12 stage 0 private cases but was not accepted by its bounded public/reviewer process. Passing all-invalid future cases does not establish feature completion.
Two buildgraph releases passed all 48 private cases and were accepted. The finite synthetic suite does not establish general production correctness.

interpretation_limits: Repeated cases may expose the same defect; occurrence counts are not independent defect counts or statistical effect estimates.
Requirement tags describe intended coverage, not necessarily the observed fault. Classification follows actual command-level output differences.
Future-operation rejection causes downstream state/output mismatches; these cascades are not counted as separate established defects.
No blanket severity or production impact rating is assigned. Demonstrated practical scope is described per family.
Primary acceptance remains 3/18 globally and 2/9 for buildgraph. Supplementary handoff diagnostics are separate.

malformed_input.quote_whitespace_normalized: Reject malformed/extra/missing command fields and unknown op values with {"error":"invalid"}, never uncaught exceptions.

audit_sort.quote_whitespace_normalized: ids is sorted: put/remove/build name, entire affected closure for effective invalidate, built nodes for commit.

import_order.quote_whitespace_normalized: After full syntax validation, normalize record and dependency ordering, then replay/conflict by shared retry key, then if record count > policy.max_import return quota, then graph checks self-cycle before missing before transitive cycle.

future_domain.quote_whitespace_normalized: Commands not introduced yet are outside that milestone's input domain.

per_stage.stop_reason: Reviewer/repair limits reached; best visible candidate retained without acceptance

static_source_evidence.excerpt: storage.save(db, graph, version + 1, audit={"version": version + 1, "op": "commit", "ids": list(order)})

defect_families.title: Commit audit IDs retain build order instead of lexical order
defect_families.observed: The affected scenarios have correct plan, commit built sequence, versions, requested digests and all other recorded outputs. Only the commit audit event IDs are out of order.
defect_families.scope: Audit representation contract deviation; these cases do not demonstrate broken scheduling, duplicate ancestor builds, incorrect artifacts or failed atomicity.
defect_families.ambiguity: No material ambiguity: built uses plan order, while audit IDs explicitly use sorted order.

defect_families.title: Collection validation hashes items before checking identifier types
defect_families.observed: Two malformed-field scenarios have receipt status error and no actual output array. Malformed fields should return invalid while preserving the state established by earlier valid commands. The dependency scenario first validly creates typed with deps:[]; the plan-target scenario starts with an empty graph.
defect_families.inference: Final domain.py calls set(value) before checking dependency identifier types at 27 and set(targets) before checking plan target types at 90. Nested lists/dicts are unhashable. TypeError is inferred from source, not a captured traceback.
defect_families.scope: Malformed command handling fails at the scenario boundary. The receipt does not record which command raised.
defect_families.ambiguity: Malformed field types are explicitly in the bounded input domain. No material contract ambiguity; exact runtime exception details are unavailable.

defect_families.title: Operation dispatch hashes an unchecked operation value
defect_families.observed: Two scenarios containing list/dict operation values have receipt status error and no actual output array.
defect_families.inference: Final domain.py 36–37 tests op membership in a set without first checking string type. TypeError is source-supported, not a recorded runtime exception.
defect_families.scope: Malformed operation handling; policy-read-shapes does not establish wrong policy/export values.
defect_families.ambiguity: The contract requires invalid for malformed/unknown operations and prohibits uncaught exceptions. Exact failing command is not recorded.

defect_families.title: Import validation rejects allowed digits in identifiers
defect_families.observed: Six valid n 0..n 5 records return invalid instead of importing. Seven valid-shaped n 0..n 6 records with missing prerequisites return invalid instead of quota.
defect_families.inference: service.py 105/116 uses ch < 'a' or ch > 'z' and not ch.isdigit() and ch != '-'. Digits and hyphens satisfy its first disjunct.
defect_families.scope: Valid import identifier rejection, not evidence of retaining the old quota: recorded policy correctly reports max_import 6 and source reads the passed policy.
defect_families.ambiguity: Allowed identifier regex and import type/range inheritance are explicit; no material ambiguity.

defect_families.title: Import graph checks precede receipt conflict and quota
defect_families.observed: Seven records return missing instead of quota. A changed manifest reusing a stored key returns missing instead of conflict. All other recorded outputs in both scenarios match.
defect_families.inference: service.py 154–168 validates the graph during normalization before receipt/quota checks at 298–306.
defect_families.scope: Error precedence deviation; recorded graph/cache/audit state is preserved. No partial import mutation is demonstrated.
defect_families.ambiguity: Syntax, replay/conflict, quota, then graph ordering is explicit; no material ambiguity.

defect_families.title: Planning pre-populates digests and loses commit built-node bookkeeping
defect_families.observed: Commits persist correct digests and versions but return built:[] instead of the nonempty plan order and record empty commit audit IDs. Retries replay the same incorrect receipt.
defect_families.inference: service.py _plan_order writes loaded graph digests at 89. Commit calls it at 130, appends to built only for still-null digests at 133–136, then audits/stores the empty list at 140–142.
defect_families.scope: Attempted but incomplete third-milestone response/audit defect. A standalone plan mutates only a local dictionary and performs no storage.save; no persisted read side effect is established. Replaying the same incorrect receipt is not a separate idempotency defect.
defect_families.ambiguity: Return built:[plan order] and audit built nodes are explicit; no material ambiguity.

defect_families.title: Final scoring applies future contracts to an early-stop selected source
defect_families.observed: Earlier-milestone selected sources reject later build/invalidate, plan/commit/audit, or import/export/policy commands as invalid. Later missing targets, retained caches, stale versions or absent audit rows frequently follow those unsupported commands.
defect_families.scope: Unmet final project requirements remain primary failures. They are not independent demonstrated regressions in implemented future features.
defect_families.ambiguity: Final evaluation intentionally applies all milestone cases. Interpretation must respect the attempted milestone. Passing future all-invalid scenarios does not demonstrate future functionality.
